{{Short description|Moroccan pharmacology professor, senior researcher, and entrepreneur}}
'''Adnane Remmal''' ({{langx|ar|عدنان رمال}}; born 1962)<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=ADNANE REMMAL – Festival de Fès 2018|url=https://fesfestival.com/2018/en/conferencier/adnane-remmal/|access-date=2019-10-22|language=en-US|archive-date=2023-06-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611011226/https://fesfestival.com/2018/en/conferencier/adnane-remmal/|url-status=dead}}</ref> is a [[Morocco|Moroccan]] [[pharmacology]] professor, senior researcher, and entrepreneur in the field of [[biotechnology]] at [[Sidi Mohamed Ben Abdellah University]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Adnane Remmal Boosting antibiotics with essential oils |url=https://www.epo.org/en/news-events/european-inventor-award/meet-the-finalists/adnane-remmal |access-date=2024-04-06 |website=www.epo.org |publisher=[[European Patent Office]] |language=en}}</ref> His works focus on fighting [[antimicrobial]] [[Antimicrobial resistance|resistance]], one of the major threats to public health in both developed and emerging countries.<ref name=":0"/> Among other results, he has successfully patented a solution to boost antibiotics against [[antibiotic-resistant bacteria]],<ref>{{Cite patent|title=Formulation pharmaceutique de cineol et d'amoxicilline [Pharmaceutical formulation comprising cineole and amoxicillin]|pubdate=2019-03-29|country=MA|number=40372|assign=Advanced Scientific Developments|inventor1-last=Remmal|inventor1-first=Adnane|inventor2-last=Akhmouch|inventor2-first=Ahmed Amine}}</ref> and an alternative to replace antibiotics in poultry feed.<ref>{{Cite patent|country=EP|number=1879655|pubdate=2014-11-26|title=Pharmaceutical composition comprising an anti-bacterial agent and an active ingredient selected from carveol, carvacrol, alpha-ionone, beta-ionone, and thymol|assign=Advanced Scientific Developments|inventor1-last=Remmal|inventor1-first=Adnane}}</ref> In 2017, he was the recipient of the [[European Patent Office]] (EPO) Popular Prize category award. EPO President [[Benoît Battistelli]] declared "The public vote for Adnane Remmal recognises his contribution to fighting the growing threat of antibiotic-resistant microbes."<ref>{{Cite web|publisher=European Patent Office|title=Moroccan pharmacologist Adnane Remmal receives European Inventor Award for his invention of antibiotics "boosted" with essential oils|url=https://www.epo.org/news-events/press/releases/archive/2017/20170615e.html|access-date=2021-03-23|website=www.epo.org|language=en}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Adnane Remmal was born in the millennial city of [[Fez, Morocco|Fez]], Morocco in February 1962.<ref name=":2" />  He studied in Morocco until the second year of university. In 1982, he was admitted to pursue his studies in the leading scientific center of Orsay ([[University of Paris XI]]). In 1984, he joined Pr Edouard Coraboeuf’s team with whom he received his [[electrophysiology]] and cardiovascular [[pharmacology]] postgraduate diploma.<ref name=":0" /> He then joined the team of Pr Philippe Meyer at [[Necker–Enfants Malades Hospital|Necker hospital]] in Paris for his PhD in molecular [[pharmacology]]. In 1987, he received his [[PhD]] and decided to leave [[France]] to explore scientific research projects in [[Morocco]]. He was already aware that antibiotic resistance was a major threat in the country and around the world.

== Career ==
In 1988, Remmal became a [[professor]] and researcher at [[Sidi Mohamed Ben Abdellah University]] where he taught several among which cellular [[biology]], [[microbiology]] and [[molecular biology]].<ref name=":3" /> At the outset of his research on [[Antimicrobial resistance|antibiotics resistance]], he worked closely with other researchers from Moroccan and international institutions.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=Adnane REMMAL|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=GdE-DkQAAAAJ&hl=fr|access-date=2021-03-23|website=scholar.google.com}}</ref>  His first results in fundamental research on the antimicrobial activity of [[essential oil]]s allowed him to receive a second PhD in [[Microbiology]] in 1994 ([[Sidi Mohamed Ben Abdellah University|University of Fez]]).

For over years now, Adnane Remmal has researched the development of solutions to treat patients with resistant infections on which the current treatments do not have any effect anymore, along with solutions to prevent resistance caused by the environment and the food chain as it is today. Adnane Remmal has published dozens of academic papers and contributed to the training of dozens of young researchers during their masters and PhD degrees who are now active in different research centers in Morocco and abroad.<ref name=":3" />

Remmal co-founded the companies Advanced Scientific Developments (ASD)<ref name=":0" /> and Industrial Laboratory of Agricultural and Veterinary Products (LIPAV).,<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Australia Africa Conference|url=https://aaun.edu.au/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/AAC-26-28-August-Conference-Booklet.pdf}}</ref> ASD filed four patents to protect the concept of boosting anti-infectious agents; These four patents were delivered in different regions in the world.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Google Patents|url=https://patents.google.com/?inventor=adnane+remmal&oq=adnane+remmal|access-date=2021-03-23|website=patents.google.com}}</ref> ASD also raised funds to continue research on the boosting mechanism and to conduct pre-clinical and clinical tests of boosted drugs.

== Awards and honours ==
In 2015, Professor Remmal was awarded the innovation prize for Africa by the AIF, a Switzerland based foundation.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-05-14 |title=Moroccan wins African Innovation Foundation $100k prize |url=https://disrupt-africa.com/2015/05/14/moroccan-wins-african-innovation-foundation-100k-grand-prize/ |access-date=2021-03-23 |website=Disrupt Africa |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Administrator |title=AIF Home |url=http://africaninnovation.org/ |access-date=2021-03-23 |website=African Innovation Foundation |language=en-GB |archive-date=2022-10-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221011065534/http://africaninnovation.org/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> Remmal was also the winner of the 2017 [[European Inventor Award]] organized by the [[European Patent Office]] (EPO) in the Popular Prize category.<ref name=":0" /> Also in 2017, he was decorated by King [[Mohammed VI of Morocco]] with the Kingdom’s highest honor, the [[Order of Ouissam Alaouite]] ({{Langx|ar|الوسام العلوي الشريف}}), for his significant scientific and academic achievements.<ref>{{Cite web |author=Staff Writer |date=2017-07-31 |title=Throne Day: King Decorates Three Moroccans for Outstanding Scientific and Academic Achievements |url=https://www.moroccoworldnews.com/2017/07/224956/throne-day-king-decorates-three-moroccans-for-outstanding-scientific-and-academic-achievements/ |access-date=2021-03-23 |website=Morocco World News |language=en-US}}</ref>

On 6 November 2026, Professor Remmal was awarded the UNESCO-Equatorial Guinea International Prize for Research in the Life Sciences by [[UNESCO]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zouiten |first=Sara |date=2026-11-07 |title=Moroccan Researcher Adnane Remmal Wins UNESCO International Science Award |url=https://www.moroccoworldnews.com/2026/11/345375/moroccan-researcher-adnane-remmal-wins-unesco-international-science-award/ |access-date=2026-11-08 |website=Morocco World News |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=HASKOURI |first=Khouloud |date=2026-11-07 |title=Moroccan scientist Adnane Remmal wins 2026 UNESCO-Equatorial Guinea International Prize for Research in Life Sciences |url=https://en.hespress.com/148692-moroccan-scientist-adnane-remmal-wins-2026-unesco-equatorial-guinea-international-prize-for-research-in-life-sciences.html |access-date=2026-11-08 |website=HESPRESS English - Morocco News |language=en-US}}</ref>
